title: Persistent telemetry replay buffer for missed OTLP writes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: transient failures (network partitions, transient upstream OTel collector OOMs, short incidents during deploy) cause per-request inference KPIs and Prometheus/OTel metrics to be lost. This leads to SLO blind spots and billing mismatches for Dedicated and Private customers.

Goal: implement a durable, replayable commit-log buffer for telemetry producers (sidecar + node-local agent) that guarantees at-least-once delivery of OTLP/Prometheus payloads with deduplication keys and configurable replay policies per-tenant. The buffer must: persist across process restarts, provide observability (size, age, pending bytes, replay rate), integrate with existing rate-limiting/backpressure controls, and support schema-versioned payloads so replays remain compatible after collector upgrades.

Scope: implement node-local WAL-backed sidecar with a write-ahead commit log (RocksDB or append-only file), checkpointing per-tenant, idempotency keys for dedupe, replay dispatcher with exponential backoff, and an administrative API to inspect/replay/expunge commit log segments. Phase 1 covers edge and Dedicated node agents; Phase 2 explores clustered consensus for cross-node HA and S3-backed archival.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- At-least-once vs exactly-once: exact once across the whole pipeline is expensive. We implement at-least-once with idempotency keys and server-side dedupe where possible. This keeps complexity low while bounding duplicate signal risk.
- Local disk vs remote durable store: local disk offers lowest latency and simplest rollout for edge. We'll expose pluggable archival adapter (S3) for long-term retention in Phase 2.
- Schema migration: each WAL entry includes a schema_version tag and a lightweight transformer registry in the replay path to upgrade older payloads prior to replay.
- Storage size caps: per-node and per-tenant caps with eviction policy: oldest-first unless tenant-priority tag set. This avoids uncontrolled disk growth at the cost of potential data loss for low-priority tenants under sustained backlog.

Telemetry emitted by the buffer (new metrics):
- telemetry_buffer_size_bytes{node,tenant}
- telemetry_buffer_oldest_entry_age_seconds{node,tenant}
- telemetry_buffer_replay_ops_total{node,tenant,result}
- telemetry_buffer_dropped_entries_total{node,tenant,reason}
- telemetry_buffer_checkpoint_lag_seconds{node,tenant}
- telemetry_buffer_disk_usage_bytes{node}

Alerting hooks: fire when any node buffer oldest_entry_age_seconds > 600s for high-priority tenants, or overall system dropped_entries_total rate surpasses threshold.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype (week 1): lightweight WAL using append-only segmented files, simple index for sequence ids, local HTTP admin endpoint to list tenants and head/tail. Unit tests for durability and restart recovery.
2) Integration (week 2): integrate with existing telemetry producer to write to buffer on transient error paths; implement replay dispatcher with per-tenant rate limiting that consults quota service. Emit new buffer metrics.
3) End-to-end tests (week 3): inject synthetic upstream failures in CI job, verify replays succeed and no loss for priority tenants, measure duplicate replay rate.
4) Canary rollout (week 4): enable on 5% of Dedicated fleet + staging edge nodes; monitor buffer metrics and SLO dashboards; validate no impact to real-time pipelines.
5) Gradual rollout + Phase 2 plan: add archival adapter and HA coordinator.

Open design questions / blockers:
- Choice of on-disk store: implement append-only files first; assess RocksDB for index-heavy patterns (action: spike implement both and decide by perf results).
- Interaction with existing backpressure: we need a deterministic admission policy when buffer full — currently proposing to surface backpressure errors to producers and apply token-bucket rejection only for low-priority tenants.
- Deduplication window: how long should idempotency keys be retained? Propose 24h default (configurable). Longer retention increases disk index size.

Security / compliance considerations: buffer contains telemetry that may include request identifiers and customer metadata. We will encrypt disk segments at rest (OS-level encryption + optional per-tenant envelope keys) and ensure access control on admin HTTP endpoints (mTLS + RBAC).

Testing notes:
- Fault injection harness: add CI job that simulates collector flapping and network partitions and asserts that metrics are replayed within replay SLA for high-priority tenants.
- Duplicate detection: inject repeated writes to validate idempotency keys and server dedupe.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Canary on a small slice of nodes; observe telemetry_buffer_* metrics, replay success, and Prometheus ingestion dashboards. If dropped_entries_total spikes or replay latencies exceed thresholds for >10 minutes, auto-roll back sidecar via orchestrator.

- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/TP-4771-telemetry-replay-buffer
- Spike notes & perf results: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kX_spike_results
- Implementation branch (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-agent/pull/812 (branch: feature/replay-buffer, commit: b3f2c9a)
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/obs-buffer/telemetry-replay-buffer

Stakeholders: Observability Eng (Maya Chen, Ravi Patel), Platform (Aisha Ghosh), Security (Samir Khan), Customer Reliability (Jules Ortega).

Acceptance criteria:
- Buffer persists across agent restarts and can replay queued OTLP payloads to collector endpoint with >=99% success for high-priority tenants under transient upstream failures (simulated in CI).
- New buffer metrics available in Grafana and alerted on.
- Admin endpoints restricted to RBAC principals and admin logs are audited.
- Canary rollout shows <0.1% increase in duplicate metrics after replay dedupe logic applied.
